newsitem.title: INDIA: India's HUDCO to launch bonds worth 2.0 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India's HUDCO to launch bonds worth 2.0 bln rupees.

text.p: India's state-owned Housing and Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) said on Thursday it will launch bonds for two billion rupees ($55.87 million) later this month to spur investment in the infrastructure sector.

"To part finance its thurst into infrastructure finance HUDCO is issuing infrastructure bonds to the tune of 2.0 billion with an option to retain oversubscription up to an additional 500 million rupees," the company said in a statement.
It said the bonds will carry an interest rate of 15 percent. The minimum investment will be fore 5,000 rupees, and any further investment would be in multiples of 1,000 rupees.
"Investment in these bonds is also availabe for NRIs (non-resident Indians) on both repatriation and non-repatriation basis," said V. Suresh, HUDCO's chairman and managing director.
The statement said the bonds will have exclusive tax benefits and they will offer instant liquidity through listing in the National Stock Exchange and the Delhi Stock Exchange.

The issue will open in the second half of March, and HUDCO will ensure that the allotment is made before the end of March so that the tax benefits would be available in the current financial year ending on March 31, 1996.
HUDCO is making arrangements to provide depositary services for the bonds through National Securities Depositary Ltd.
The issue is being lead-managed by SBI Capital Markets, JM Financial, DSP Merrill Lynch and Kotak Mahindra.
HUDCO was established in 1970 and has an equity base of 3.24 billion rupees. ($1 - 35.8 rupees)
